Halving LR undertrained — cosine annealing from 1e-2 decays to 0 across 8 epochs, leaving the model far from its loss minimum. LR=2e-2 confirmed as a good initial rate. Original LR restored.

summary: Lower clip floor for w[11] (LT fail_d_exp) and w[20] (ST fail_d_exp) from 0.001 to 0.0.

summary: Sharpen recency curve exponent: weight = C0 + C1 * (review_ord/N)^5 (was ^3).

Same lesson as iter 18: re-weighting training away from the natural distribution trades one bucket for another and net-hurts eval LL. The recency win (iter 4/14) was special because the test split genuinely is the most-recent time chunk; arbitrary class/time reweighting lacks that distribution-match justification.

summary: STRUCTURAL: slip/guess recall calibration. Add w[35]=slip, w[36]=guess; p_cal = guess + (1-guess-slip)*retention, applied only to the prediction (internal retention for stability unchanged). Enzyme rebuild.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: IRT-style floor/ceiling to attack the dominant Again loss. Improvement +0.00031 < threshold 0.0004 (2 new params * 0.0002). Per-param: slip median 0.0094 (21pct at floor 0), guess median 0.0535 (reaches 0.3 ceiling for some). Slip (ceiling) drives the Again win by lowering overconfident predictions; guess (floor) slightly HURT easy (0.1613->0.1626). Next: drop guess, keep slip-only (1 param, threshold halves to 0.0002, sheds guess collateral damage).

summary: STRUCTURAL: difficulty-dependent forgetting curve. Add w[35]=d_weight; scale the slow-forgetting mixture component by exp(d_weight*(D-5)) in fsrs7_forgetting_curve. Enzyme rebuild.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: D never shaped the curve before, only S did; endpoint/monotonicity stay safe because the mixture weights remain >0. Improvement +0.000305 > threshold 0.0002 (1 new param, 1.5x). Win comes from the recall classes (easy 0.1613->0.1599, good 0.1429->0.1421, hard 0.1288->0.1285), NOT Again (flat 1.4008->1.4010). d_weight median -0.068, fully interior (0.2pct at floor, 0pct ceiling) -> genuine learned signal, not L2-at-bound artifact. Negative sign => hard cards (D>5) forget faster (steeper curve), easy cards slower -> matches cognitive-science prediction. Complexity +0.03pct. New champion at iter 23.

summary: STRUCTURAL: empirical-Bayes L2 prior. Shrink each (user,split) param row toward the live population mean (flat_fsrs_params.mean(dim=0), detached, recomputed per step) instead of the fixed FSRS7_DEFAULT anchor. Threaded anchor_p through train_iter -> masked_penalty -> penalty_loss; sigmas and PENALTY_W_L2 unchanged. 0 new params, no rebuild.
comment: Improvement +0.000132 > threshold 0.0001 (1.32x). Attacks the dominant cross-iteration pattern: bound-saturated params are L2-anchored at their own fixed default, several sitting exactly on a clamp (w[25] default 2.5==floor, ~9pct pinned; w[29] default 0.5==floor, ~22pct pinned). Replacing the fixed anchor with the live population centroid lets the population drift to where the data collectively wants it while still regularizing individual outliers; at init anchor==FSRS7_DEFAULT so it is a strict generalization of prior behavior. Win broad across recall classes (good 0.14210->0.14184, easy ~0.1599->0.15949, hard ~0.1285->0.12856); Again slightly worse (1.4010->1.4019) but outweighed (recall classes ~128M of 152M reviews). No leakage: anchor computed only from train-fit params, never touches test. Complexity +0.10pct. New champion at iter 24. Follow-ups: (a) alternative hypothesis 'L2 simply too strong' -> probe lower PENALTY_W_L2/raised sigma; (b) empirical-Bayes prior VARIANCE (sigma_j from population std); (c) per-split anchor.

summary: Restore learnable difficulty mean-reversion rate: replace the hardcoded 0.01 in fsrs7_mean_reversion with trainable w[36]=mr_rate (default 0.01, bounds [0,1], sigma 0.2). Enzyme rebuild.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: a standard FSRS degree of freedom this fork had pinned. Improvement -0.000092 (WORSE) < threshold 0.0002. The param was NOT dead: median moved 4x off default to 0.0415 (10.6pct at floor 0, p99 0.31) with strong gradient (|g|~15.7), so the optimizer actively wanted MORE reversion than the hardcoded 0.01. But test by_user got worse: it traded a small recall-class gain (hard 0.12856->0.12801, easy 0.15949->0.15927) for a larger Again increase (1.40187->1.40263). Net negative => the extra per-user DOF overfits the train distribution (which differs from the recency-weighted, most-recent test chunk); the hardcoded 0.01 generalizes better. LESSON: difficulty *dynamics* params sit upstream of the prediction and overfit when freed per-user under a weak prior; confirms the pre-run 'upstream/diluted' hypothesis. Don't free difficulty-trajectory params per-user without much stronger reg (or tie them GLOBAL/shared). The param HAS train-signal but it's not generalizable. Next: pivot back to a DIRECT curve-shape change (D-modulate the slow-component decay), which hits p like the iter-23 win.

summary: STRUCTURAL: D-modulated forgetting-curve SHAPE. Add w[36]=d_decay; in fsrs7_forgetting_curve scale the slow component's decay: decay2_mag = clamp(decay2*exp(d_decay*(D-5)), 0.01, 0.95), decay2=-decay2_mag. Protective clamp prevents base^(1/decay) float overflow. Enzyme rebuild.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: distinct mechanism from iter-23 d_weight (curve SHAPE vs mixture WEIGHT). Improvement +0.000321 > threshold 0.0002 (1.6x). Bigger than the iter-24 EB win, comparable to iter-23. d_decay median +0.083 (interior; 1.9pct hit upper 0.3, 0.4pct lower) => genuine learned signal: positive sign means hard cards (D>5) get a STEEPER slow tail (forget faster), which agrees with iter-23 d_weight's negative sign (same cognitive direction, cross-validates). FIRST curve change to move AGAIN: again 1.40187->1.40063 (-0.0012), plus good 0.14184->0.14173, easy 0.15949->0.15917; hard ~flat (+0.0001). Long-term reviews improved most (0.32526->0.32490). The shape lever reaches the failure/long-tail region the weight lever didn't. Numerically safe via the [0.01,0.95] clamp (Enzyme autodiffs fsrs7_clamp fine; d_decay=0 recovers champion exactly). Complexity +0.03pct. New champion at iter 26. Note: ~2pct of users push d_decay to the 0.3 upper bound -- could widen to 0.4 later, but median well interior so low priority. Open: combine d_weight+d_decay are both interior and both 'hard forgets faster' -- the D->curve axis is productive; next maybe D-modulate the FAST component decay1 (short-term/low-S region) or the clean EB prior-variance swing.

summary: D-modulate the FAST component decay: add w[37]=d_decay1; decay1_mag = clamp(decay1*exp(d_decay1*(D-5)), 0.01, 0.95). Enzyme rebuild.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: mirror of iter-26 on the slow component; targets the short-term region. Improvement +0.000198 < threshold 0.0002 (0.99x) -- NEAR MISS by 0.0000024. Real attributable signal but doesn't clear the +1-param bar. d_decay1 median -0.043 (interior; 0.09pct floor, 0.41pct ceiling) -- crucially OPPOSITE sign to iter-26 d_decay (slow, +0.083): the fast and slow curve components want opposite-direction D-modulation, so they CANNOT be tied into one shared param (rules out the cheap 0-new-param reformulation). Per-class: BIGGEST Again move yet (1.40063->1.39803, -0.0026) and short_term improved (-0.00068, as hypothesized: fast component governs short intervals), but recall classes got worse (good +0.00018, easy +0.00031) and long_term flat -- net just under threshold. The fast-component D-shape DOF trades recall accuracy for failure/short- term accuracy; can't isolate the Again gain without per-class params (forbidden, see iter 18). DECISION (near-miss discretion): signal is intrinsic to this DOF (interior, not bound-limited; tying ruled out by opposite sign; no obvious cheaper reformulation), so NOT worth chasing -- move on. The D->curve axis is now mined (slow-weight iter23 + slow-decay iter26 accepted; fast-decay sub-threshold). Next: pivot to the unexplored transition function w[25..26].

summary: Raise base2 (w[30]) forgetting-curve ceiling 0.99 -> 0.998. Python-only (FSRS_MAX + diagnostics), no rebuild.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: 16.9% of users pinned at the 0.99 ceiling with the highest gradient (~29) of any bounded curve param, and default 0.9555 != ceiling (genuine data strain, not L2-at-default); base2<1 keeps p(inf)=0. Improvement +0.0000298 < threshold 0.0001 (0.30x). Bound relaxation barely moved the needle despite the high gradient + 16.9pct ceiling strain. Per-class: recall classes improved (easy 0.15917->0.15888, good 0.14173->0.14153, hard 0.12865->0.12841) but AGAIN got WORSE (1.4006->1.4018, +0.0012): a flatter slow tail over-predicts retention -- helps when the card is recalled, hurts when it lapses -- so net is only +0.00003. KEY LESSON: a high gradient AT a bound does NOT mean the CLAMP is the binding constraint. base2 has a TIGHT L2 prior (sigma 0.068) anchored at the EB population mean ~0.93; THAT co-binds at the ceiling, so relaxing only the clamp leaves the L2 pulling users back toward 0.93 and they barely move past 0.99. Refined rule for bound probes: check whether the L2 sigma (not the clamp) is the true binding force. DECISION (near-miss discretion): reject + revert; chasing base2 higher would need loosening its sigma too, but the Again/recall tradeoff suggests low ceiling on the upside. Move on. Compaction now due (delta 5).

summary: Per-time-fold empirical-Bayes anchor: shrink each (user,split) row toward its OWN time-fold's population mean (per_fold_mean[split_indices]) instead of the global mean over all folds (iter-24). 0 new params, no rebuild. NOTE: complexity baseline dropped 18764->13962 in a separate chore commit (ac2dd92) that removed dead non-SGD S0-init code (initialize_parameters/f_interpolate/bin_interval) from the FSRS7 PyTorch reference model; logloss identical, so that drop is unrelated to this iteration.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: align the EB prior with the time-split structure that recency weighting exploits. Improvement -0.0000120 (WORSE) < threshold 0.0001. Per-fold anchoring slightly helped Again (1.40061->1.40051, -0.0001) but hurt the recall classes (good 0.14173->0.14177, easy 0.15917->0.15921, +0.00004 each) and long-term (0.32490->0.32492); net by_user worse. LESSON: the iter-24 EB win came from POOLING STRENGTH -- a single low-variance centroid over all user x fold rows regularizes the recall-class params well -- NOT from fold-specific targeting. Splitting the anchor per time-fold shrinks the data behind each centroid and removes cross-fold information sharing, weakening the regularization. The population's optimal params are effectively stable across time-folds; the time-distribution shift is already handled at the GRADIENT level by recency weighting (iters 4/14), so duplicating it in the prior centroid is redundant and slightly harmful. Reverted to the global-mean anchor (iter-24 champion). complexity_before 13962 = post-chore baseline (dead S0-init code removed in ac2dd92).

summary: STRUCTURAL: stability-modulated FAST-component decay. Add w[37]=s_decay1; in fsrs7_forgetting_curve scale the fast component's decay by a power of S: decay1_mag = clamp(decay1 * S^s_decay1, 0.01, 0.95), decay1=-decay1_mag. Default 0 recovers champion exactly. Enzyme rebuild.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: mirror of iter-26 (d_decay on the slow component) but driven by S, which naturally gates the fast component to the short-term (small-S) regime; targets the elevated short-term loss (0.357 vs 0.325 long-term). Improvement +0.000581 > threshold 0.0002 (2.9x) -- biggest single-iter win since the early recency work, and the largest Again move of any iteration. w[37]=s_decay1 median -0.045, fully INTERIOR (0.2%/0.2% at bounds), strong gradient (|g| 5.27 all / 4.70 last) => genuine learned signal, not a bound artifact. Mechanism confirmed: negative s_decay1 makes the FAST component's decay STEEPER at small S (S^neg > 1 for S<1 day), so short-term (sub-day) predictions get lower, less-overconfident retention. The win lands exactly where hypothesized: Again 1.40061->1.39257 (-0.00804, the dominant-loss class), short-term 0.35708->0.35497 (-0.00211); long-term ~flat (-0.00011). Recall classes regressed slightly (good 0.14173->0.14227 +0.00054, easy 0.15918->0.15956 +0.00038, hard +0.00024) but are vastly outweighed (Again is 23.7M reviews; by_user net -0.00058, by_review agrees -0.00086). KEY vs iter-27 (D-mod fast decay, near-miss): using S instead of D gates the modulation to short-term because the fast component is negligible at high S (slow:fast ~280:1 at S=1000), so it barely touches recall/long-term -- this solves iter-27's recall-coupling failure. Endpoints p(0)=1, p(inf)=0 preserved (clamp [0.01,0.95] + base1<1 => factor1>0, monotone). Complexity +0.04% (13962->13968). New champion at iter 30.

summary: S-modulate the SLOW component's decay: add w[38]=s_decay2; decay2_mag = clamp(decay2 * exp(d_decay*(D-5)) * S^s_decay2, 0.01, 0.95). Enzyme rebuild.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: mirror of iter-30 on the slow component; completes the decay-modulation family (fast/slow x D/S). The slow component dominates at high S, so this targets the long-term tail. Improvement +0.0000753 < threshold 0.0002 (0.38x) -- NEAR MISS, real but small. w[38]=s_decay2 median +0.026 (near zero), interior (0.4%/0.3% at bounds) but WEAK gradient (|g| 1.34 vs s_decay1's 5.22): the slow component barely wants S-modulation. This is the mirror image of iter-30's big win and the contrast IS the lesson -- short-term (fast component) had large loss headroom (0.357) so S-modulating fast decay won +0.00058; long-term (slow component) is more saturated (0.325) AND the slow component's S-behaviour is already richly captured by its S-power weight (s_weight_power2), so S-modulating the slow decay adds little. Broad tiny gains (Again 1.39257->1.39192, long-term 0.32479->0.32468 -0.00011) but net well under the +1-param bar. DECISION (near-miss): reject + revert to the iter-30 champion. The signal is intrinsic to the param (cannot cheapen -- fast and slow want independent S-dependence, so s_decay1/s_decay2 can't be tied) and long-term is saturated, so not worth chasing. The decay-modulation family is now fully mapped: D-weight-slow (iter23 WON), D-decay-slow (iter26 WON), D-decay-fast (iter27 near-miss), S-decay-fast (iter30 WON big), S-decay-slow (iter31 near-miss); weight S-mods are redundant with s_weight_power. Next: pivot off curve modulations to a different structure.

summary: STRUCTURAL: add a 3rd (short-term) forgetting-curve mixture component. New params decay3(38), base3(39), base_weight3(40); R3=(1+factor3*t/s)^(-decay3), weight3=base_weight3*s^(-s_weight_power1) (S-profile tied to the fast component so it concentrates at small S). base_weight3=0 recovers the 2-component champion. Enzyme rebuild.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: targets residual short-term loss (0.355 vs 0.325 long-term). Improvement +0.0000693 << threshold 0.0006 (0.12x) -- decisive reject. The 3rd component barely activated: base_weight3 median 0.086 (vs base_weight1 ~0.22, base_weight2 ~0.65) with 16.9% of users driving it to 0 (off); decay3 settled at 0.152, base3 0.594. Even with full freedom and an S-profile aimed at the short-term region, a 3rd timescale moved by_user only +0.00007 -- nowhere near the 3-param bar. CONCLUSION: the 2-component power-law mixture is structurally COMPLETE. Combined with the modulation map (D-weight iter23 / D-decay iter26 / S-decay-fast iter30 accepted; D-decay-fast iter27 / S-decay-slow iter31 near-miss; weight-mods redundant with s_weight_power; base-mods numerically infeasible via base^(1/decay) overflow), the forgetting-curve surface is now FULLY MINED. Reverted to iter-30 champion. Next: pivot OFF the curve -- remaining frontiers are a new state variable (short-term memory trace; +0.0010 threshold, heavy CUDA/Enzyme work) or a different training/regularization structure.

summary: L2-sigma empirical-Bayes calibration, STD variant (user idea): set each regularized param's L2 sigma proportional to its EMPIRICAL population std across the trained (user,split) rows, strength-normalized (x1.636) so the champion's total L2 penalty mass (params 4-35) is preserved. init-S (w0-3) left unregularized at 9999. 0 new params, complexity-neutral.
comment: Pre-reg hypothesis: isolate the per-param SHAPE of the prior from its overall strength. REJECT (bar +0.0001, 0-param training-hyperparameter change, complexity-neutral). by_user 0.32106495 -> 0.32114062 = -0.0000757 (WORSE); by_review 0.33450 -> 0.33463 (also worse). Setting sigma_i proportional to the empirical posterior std (strength-matched to the champion so only the SHAPE changes) is worse than the hand-set sigmas. This is the classic empirical-Bayes pitfall: the spread of the per-user posteriors measured UNDER a loose prior OVERESTIMATES the true between-user variance because it also absorbs within-user estimation noise (data-starved users scatter). So sigma~std wrongly LOOSENS the priors on the highest-apparent-variance params (letting noisy low-data users overfit them more) and over-tightens the genuinely-converged low-variance params -- both directions hurt. The hand-tuned sigmas (evolved across the campaign) evidently encode a better shape than the raw posterior spread. Magnitude is small (~8e-5) so the prior shape is a second-order lever, consistent with the model being near a good prior already. Reverted to iter-54 champion (0.321065). Next: the robust MAD variant (iter-61) -- 1.4826*MAD is smaller than std exactly on the heavy-tailed params (idx 18/22/23/24 std/MAD up to 6x), so it tightens (not loosens) the noisy params, the opposite correction, and may land differently.

REJECT (bar +0.0001, 0-param training-hyperparameter change, complexity-neutral). by_user 0.32106495 -> 0.32145604 = -0.000391 (much WORSE); by_review 0.33450 -> 0.33479. Paired with iter-60 the result is cleanly MONOTONIC: champion 0.3210649 > std-shape 0.3211406 (-7.6e-5) > MAD-shape 0.3214560 (-3.9e-4) -- the harder you push the prior shape toward 'sigma proportional to empirical posterior spread', the worse by_user gets. MAD is even worse than std because it is smaller than std exactly on the heavy-tailed params (idx 18/22/23/24, std/MAD up to 6x), so after strength-normalization (k_mad=3.582) it pushes those to very tight sigma and the clean params to very loose sigma -- a MORE extreme version of the same wrong shape. CONCLUSION: empirical posterior spread (std or MAD) is a BAD prior-scale estimator here. Under a loose prior the per-user posterior spread overestimates the true between-user variance by absorbing within-user estimation noise (data-starved users scatter), so 'more apparent spread' does NOT mean 'deserves more prior freedom'. The hand-tuned sigmas, evolved across the campaign, are already better-shaped; this lever is now thoroughly tested and dead in the EB-spread direction. (Strength was held constant by construction, so this is a SHAPE verdict only; the global L2 strength axis is PENALTY_W_L2, separately owned by hp_tune, already at its tuned 0.75.) Reverted to iter-54 champion (0.321065). Each shrinks to its OWN population mean (bw1~0.21, bw2~0.65), so the joint shrinkage regularizes the identifiable weight RATIO toward a good population value; with bw2 fixed at 1.0, bw1 alone must both carry the ratio AND be regularized by a single mean-anchored prior, which is a strictly weaker / differently-centered regularizer on the ratio. So the covariance idea worked as a REDUNDANCY DETECTOR (found a real prediction-time scale degeneracy via the -0.72 correlation), but the degeneracy is not removable without loss because the EB-L2 prior makes both DOF functionally useful for ratio shrinkage.
